source.title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons

accepted.question_text: In electron-positron annihilation into hadrons, why is the pion-pair Bose-Einstein-correlation emitter dimension rππ, where r is the Gaussian source-size parameter in the two-boson correlation C₂(Q) = 1 + λ₂ exp(-r²Q²) with Q² = -(p₁ - p₂)², essentially independent of the center-of-mass energy √s_ee even though the average hadron multiplicity increases with energy; and what source model can quantitatively account for that flat rππ distribution?
accepted.context_brief: flat energy dependence of pion BEC source radius in e+e− annihilation

evidence.quote: Assuming the emitter to be a sphere of a Gaussian distribution, the correlation of pairs of identical bosons can be parametrised by C2(Q) = 1 + λ2e−r2Q2 where Q2 = −(p1 − p2)2 and p1 and p2 are the four momenta of the two bosons.

As for the rππ values obtained from the e+e− annihilation analyses, they are seen in Fig. 1 to be essentially independent of √see as it is generally accepted that the small deviations from a constant value are due to the non-uniformity of the chosen experimental procedures. Since e.g. the average hadron multiplicity increases with energy this flat r distribution poses a theoretical challenge.
As seen, the r behaviour extracted from this simplified model, which rises by only ∼3.5% from 10 to 90 GeV CM energy, already describes nicely experimental situation.

accepted.question_text: In hadronic Z⁰ decays studied with Bose-Einstein correlations for identical boson pairs and Fermi-Dirac correlations for baryon pairs, what hadronization explanation can account for the observed decrease of the emitter dimension r(m) with hadron mass, from about 0.75 fm at the pion mass to about 0.15 fm at the Lambda-baryon mass, especially given that many hadronization models, including the Lund model, expect r to increase with hadron mass and that the very small Lambda emitter dimension lacks a satisfactory explanation?
accepted.context_brief: decrease of BEC/FDC emitter radius with hadron mass

evidence.quote: The very high statistics of the Z0 hadronic decay events accumulated by the LEP experiments and the extension of the BEC analysis to baryon pairs via the FDC method opened the way to study the emitter dimension rππ as a function of the hadron mass, from pions to Λ baryons.
The emitter dimension r(m) is seen to decrease with the hadron mass, from ∼0.75 fm at mπ to ∼0.15 fm at mΛ.

On the other hand, the decrease of r with the hadron mass poses a challenge to a large variety of hadronisation models, including the Lund one, which expect r to increase with the hadron mass. In particular at present, there is no satisfactory explanation for the very small rΛ value.

accepted.question_text: How can models of hadron production in electron-positron annihilation account for the approximate minimum emitter energy density inferred from BEC/FDC emitter dimensions being near 100 GeV/fm³ for proton and Lambda emitters, while pion and kaon emitters remain in a reasonable range?
accepted.context_brief: high inferred energy density of proton and Lambda emitters

evidence.quote: Consequently one may try and estimate an approximate minimum energy density of the emitter of the two hadrons

Whereas the energy density for the pion and kaon emitters still lies within a reasonable range, the energy densities of the protons and Λ’s emitters are lying in the vicinity of 100 GeV/fm3, way above the values anticipated from the current models for hadron production.

accepted.question_text: In two-dimensional Bose-Einstein-correlation analysis, where pion correlations are analyzed in the Longitudinal Centre of Mass System using longitudinal and transverse momentum-difference variables to determine a longitudinal emitter dimension r_L and transverse dimension r_T, to what extent is it valid to infer the underlying dynamics of heavy-ion collisions from r_L(m_T) when the same longitudinal-radius dependence on transverse mass m_T appears in electron-positron annihilations, which contain no nuclear matter?
accepted.context_brief: dynamical interpretation of two-dimensional BEC radii

evidence.quote: In recent years the correlations of pions emerging from heavy ion collisions and from e+e− annihilations have been analysed in terms of the 2-dimensional BEC analysis. This analysis is carried out in the Longitudinal Centre of Mass System

From a fit to the data one is able to determine the longitudinal rL and the transverse rT dimensions. The dependence of rL on mT are shown in Fig. 3 for e+e− annihilations, as measured by DELPHI at the Z0 mass, and for S+Pb collisions at 200 GeV/A as measured by the NA44 collaboration.

At this point the obvious question arises as to what extend one is permitted to extract from the 2-dimensional BEC analyses information on the underlying dynamics of heavy ion collisions when rL(mT) behaves essentially the same as the in e+e− annihilations which are void of nuclear matter.

accepted.question_text: Can Bose-Einstein correlations in high-energy hadron production be consistently generalized by imposing isospin invariance, so that a Generalised Bose-Einstein Correlation framework relates systems such as π±π± and π±π⁰, and can this GBEC framework be experimentally verified in high-energy physics?
accepted.context_brief: experimental validity of Generalised Bose-Einstein Correlations

evidence.quote: In analogue to the generalised Pauli principle, which extends that principle from two identical nucleons to the proton-neutron system, one may consider an inclusions of the isospin invariance to extend the BEC to a generalised BEC (GBEC).
Such an extension has been proposed by several authors [1] with the aim to establish BEC relations between e.g. the π±π± and π±π0 systems.
The GBEC validity at high energy physics is still an open question due to the missing of an experimental verification.

accepted.question_text: Does the observed hadron-mass dependence of the emitter dimension r(m), measured in electron-positron annihilation and decreasing with hadron mass, also occur in particle reactions other than electron-positron annihilation?

evidence.quote: The emitter dimension r(m) is seen to decrease with the hadron mass, from ∼0.75 fm at mπ to ∼0.15 fm at mΛ.
The r(m) behaviour should be investigated also in other than e+e− particles reactions

accepted.question_text: What physical interpretation should be assigned to the Bose-Einstein-correlation-derived dimension r if the hadron-mass dependence of r(m), the high inferred hadron-emitter energy densities, and the analogy with Bose condensates suggest that the relevant scale may resemble an inter-particle separation proportional to 1/√mass rather than an ordinary emitter size?
accepted.context_brief: interpretation of the BEC-derived dimension r

evidence.quote: In trying to gain an insight into the r(m) behaviour and the energy density of the hadron emitter it may be instructive to turn to other phenomena related to the Bose-Einstein statistics.
One of them are the Bose condensates where it was shown [5] that at equal very low temperature their inter-atomic separations are proportional to 1/√matom and not to their dimension.
This comparison coupled to the behaviour of r(m) and the high emitter energy densities may point to the need to re-examine the interpretation given to the BEC derived dimension r.
